source_reference: cb8081en.pdf FAOSTYLE §12.6–12.8 (pp. 56–60); project citations-rules.md rules 54–138; exemplar: References_e76e2b681_CORRECTED.md (client-supplied example of accepted FAO formatting)
applies_to: reference/bibliography lists in the author–date citation system
precedence_note: These rules implement FAOSTYLE §12.6–12.8 and rank per conflicts.md precedence: preset locks > client_override rules > FAOSTYLE > schema > termlist > OED. No rule here currently carries client_override.

constraints.label_integrity: Entry text under an [n] label may change freely; never add/renumber/reorder/delete labels. Re-sorting is done by label-preserving text swaps or deferred to DOCX stage.
constraints.quoted_material: Titles are rendered as published except where rule REF-CASE-001 applies; transliterated/translated titles follow Box 12.1.
constraints.locked_mode: Reformatting entries is an editorial fix (skill: 'reference-list formatting and ordering'); does not require author action unless a decision_point applies.

rules.rule: Element order for all entries: Author. Year. Title. Series title, Series number. Place, Publisher. URL
rules.example: Baltzer, K. & Hansen, H. 2011. Agricultural input subsidies in sub-Saharan Africa. Evaluation study. Copenhagen, DANIDA. https://... Internal document.

rules.rule: Alphabetical by author surname; corporate authors alphabetized by their abbreviation with the full name made available in parentheses at first use
More than ten authors: list first seven, remainder optionally truncated with et al.
'and' or ampersand (&) between the last two author names in each reference; FAOSTYLE examples consistently use '&'. Ampersand is banned in in-text citations (rule 23).
Bold mandatory for author names only. Wrap the entire author string in bold up to and including the period after the final author name: **Author, A.B. & Author, C.D.** Year. ...
Titles of FAO information products use sentence case (initial letter plus proper names); meetings, official days/years, projects and conferences take initial capitalization
rules.note: Applies to published titles too, e.g. 'Securing Africa's Land for Shared Prosperity' -> 'Securing Africa's land for shared prosperity'

rules.rule: Italicize titles of books, journals, papers, periodicals and websites, including foreign-language titles
Do NOT italicize titles of articles, presentations and chapters, including foreign-language titles
City (and country) of publication come BEFORE the publisher; omit the country when the city is a capital
USA and UK may be abbreviated in references; omit all other administrative detail except 'Washington, DC'
Multiple locations: one location per publisher; otherwise single location with multiple publishers
rules.example: Rome, FAO & Quebec City, Canada, CINE / Cairo, FAO, CIRAD & CIHEAM.

rules.rule: Journal format: Journal Title, volume(issue): pages. No 'vol.', 'no.', 'pp.'; article numbers replace page ranges where used by the journal
rules.example: Society and Natural Resources, 16(3): 249–263. / Land Use Policy, 120: 106255.

rules.rule: Journal titles either full or standard-abbreviated in ALL entries — never mixed
Provide the DOI as a URL; otherwise the preview page (FAO Knowledge Repository handle URL); otherwise a direct URL. No angled brackets; include http(s)://; underlining optional
Web sources: access date in square brackets before the URL, format [Cited DD Month YYYY]; databases use [Accessed on DD Month YYYY] plus Licence where applicable
Static sources (PDFs, DOIs) may omit the cited date
Web page within a website: after the piece title, 'In: Website identity.' Place. [Cited date]. URL
rules.example: World Bank. 2019. Understanding poverty. In: The World Bank. Washington, DC. [Cited 3 April 2019]. www.worldbank.org/...

rules.rule: National/supranational legislation: Country. Name of legislation, date. Codes. Optional 'Also available at: [FAOLEX URL]'. Country acts as author, so in-text citations use the country name
rules.example: Kenya. 2016. Community Land Act, No. 27 of 2016. Nairobi, Government Printer.

rules.rule: Same author, same year: suffix a, b (e.g. FAO. 2021a / 2021b); unpublished at time of writing: 'forthcoming' in both text and list

List title 'References' when all entries are cited; 'Bibliography' with subsections 'References' + 'Further reading' when uncited entries are retained; subsections permitted in heavily cited documents
Non-English sources: prefer full version in publication language; translated title in [square brackets] after original; translation-era words (forthcoming, Cited, eds.) in the publication language
First word after a colon (or en dash) in a title is capitalized
rules.faostyle: §12.8.1 examples passim ('...fish stocks: The case...'; exemplar '...pastoral lands: Implementing...')
rules.example: Governing land for women and men: A technical guide...

rules.rule: Official titles functioning as proper names retain their published capitalization (e.g. the VGGT full title); REF-CASE-001 sentence case applies to ordinary descriptive titles only
rules.faostyle: §8.1; exemplar line: FAO. 2012. *Voluntary Guidelines on the Responsible Governance of Tenure...*. Rome.
rules.decision_point: DP-2 (superseded: exemplar shows the accepted FAO practice)

rules.rule: Omit the publisher when identical to the author ('FAO. 2012. ... Rome.', never 'Rome, FAO.'); include it when author and publisher differ
rules.faostyle: §12.8.1 examples: all FAO-authored entries omit; 'Ruane, J.... Rome, FAO.' includes (authors ≠ FAO)

decision_points.question: Ampersand vs 'and' between last two authors in the reference list
decision_points.resolution: RESOLVED: '&' in reference list (FAOSTYLE example-consistent; exemplar confirms)

decision_points.question: Sentence-case official titles (rule 69) — affects the VGGT title itself [63], which reads oddly in sentence case
options: retain official title case as a proper-name exception and log a client_override
decision_points.recommendation: apply strictly but log a one-line note in conflicts.md for the client to overrule
decision_points.resolution: RESOLVED 2026-08-11: exemplar file shows accepted practice — VGGT and similar official titles keep published capitalization (encoded as REF-CASE-003); sentence case + capital after colon elsewhere

decision_points.question: Legislation with country as author (REF-LEG-001) rewrites 17 in-text citations in P16 ((Republic of Kenya, 2016) -> (Kenya, 2016) etc.)
options: reformat list entries only, keep 'Republic of ...' as author string
decision_points.recommendation: client sign-off before applying; if approved, apply both sides in one pass to keep text and list consistent
